title: Well and Choir
premise: Cyrus Sterling is hired to appraise Hollowmere House, a derelict property whose previous owners all vanished mid-survey, and whose appraisal values keep shifting upward on their own. He discovers the founders' ritual—a covenant binding the house to the town through a dry well—and that the 'found family' who once tended it were sacrificed to keep the water down. When his sleep recordings reveal a second voice answering his questions, Cyrus realizes the house has chosen him as its next keeper. He must complete the founders' unfinished ritual, but the final step requires a willing sacrifice: he offers the house his inherited name instead of his body, breaking the covenant and draining the well forever, though the voice follows him out.
about_author: Yara Zhou is the pen name of a former building inspector turned writer who spent a decade cataloguing houses no one would insure. Her fiction explores what structures remember and who pays their debts.

chapters.title: The Square Footage of Grief
chapters.summary: Cyrus, a compulsively rational surveyor estranged from his family name, arrives at Hollowmere House for a routine appraisal and finds measurements that contradict themselves by dawn. He meets the town's last caretaker, Mabel, who warns him to leave before dark. His POV establishes his armor of skepticism. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Answers in the Dark
chapters.summary: Cyrus stays overnight to verify anomalies and leaves recorders running while he sleeps. Playback reveals a second voice—dry, patient—answering his sleep-talk with truths about the founders' covenant and the well. Mabel shows him the founders' ledger: the 'found family' were fed to the water. His skepticism cracks. Emotional beat: the terror of being known.

chapters.title: What the Water Was Owed
chapters.summary: The well begins refilling as Cyrus researches the founders' unfinished ritual in the cellar. Mabel confesses she was meant to be the last keeper and fled, leaving the covenant broken. The house starts rewriting itself around Cyrus—rooms he measured now contain his childhood home's details. Climax: he descends as the well brims. Emotional beat: power seducing him into complicity.

chapters.title: Deeded
chapters.summary: At the well's edge, the voice offers Cyrus the house entire—power, permanence, belonging. He completes the ritual's final line but substitutes his inherited family name, Sterling, as the sacrifice, unmaking his claim to the legacy that brought him here. The well drains; the house goes quiet. Resolution: Cyrus leaves nameless and free, though at a motel he hears water dripping. Emotional beat: costly liberation.
